root_cause: The ChainableUndefined class incorrectly reports that an undefined value passes the `is escaped` test. In the macro, the line `"html": params.description if params.description is escaped else params.descriptionHtml` therefore selects `params.description` (which is undefined) when `params.description` is missing, leaving `description.html` undefined and causing the final output to be empty instead of falling back to `descriptionHtml`.

evidence.why: turn 1: list_dir . | turn 2: list_dir src | turn 3: run_python -> exit code 1 | turn 4: run_test -> FAILED | turn 5: submit | submitted: This test reproduces the bug where `params.description is escaped` incorrectly evaluates to True for an undefined value when using ChainableUndefined.
